content:
Santa Claus finds himself in the crosshairs of Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown in a new piece of political street art in New York.

The Christmas gift-giver is detained and searched by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents as his horrified reindeer look on in the mural by street artist Doug Groupp, aka Clown Soldier.

“The idea came out of watching the Trump administration’s increasingly aggressive immigration crackdown,” Groupp explained to HuffPost. “I wanted to take something familiar and turn it on its head. Santa Claus is probably the most recognizable figure associated with Christmas, and the idea of him being arrested by ICE struck me as both absurd and disturbing.”

“There’s a certain dark humor to it, but underneath that humor is something much more serious,” he added.

Groupp said the mural was not inspired by any single incident but by the broader climate surrounding immigration enforcement and what he sees as the normalization of fear and suspicion in the Trump era.

“Frankly, there are moments when I feel as though I’m living in a fascist state,” Groupp said. “I never imagined I’d see something like this happening in America.”

“I’m not suggesting there aren’t problems with our immigration system, but this is not how we should be addressing them,” he added. “I think we’re scapegoating some of the most vulnerable people in society. Preying on people who have little power to defend themselves is unjustifiable.”

Groupp painted the piece earlier this month at the corner of Lafayette and Broome Streets in SoHo, Manhattan, in collaboration with the L.I.S.A. Project NYC, a nonprofit that brings street art to public spaces across the Big Apple.

It follows his 2025 work “Attack on Liberty,” which depicted ICE agents arresting the Statue of Liberty.

Groupp, who has been creating street art in New York for years, said humor and satire are central to his work.

“Humor is often the most effective way I know to express the appalling contradictions I see here in the United States,” he told HuffPost.

Santa, he noted, travels across borders. “The irony of ICE arresting Santa Claus seemed almost too perfect,” he said.

Groupp said he deliberately gave the mural the appearance of a cheerful Christmas illustration.

“It’s warm, bright, colorful, and cheerful, almost like something you’d see on a Hallmark Christmas card,” he explained. “But then you notice the ICE agents arresting Santa, and suddenly the whole scene is turned upside down.”

“I love that contradiction,” he added. “The image initially appears innocent, but the longer you look at it, the more disturbing it becomes.”

Groupp said the response has been overwhelmingly positive, although the mural has also sparked criticism and heated exchanges on the street.

“Some people laugh, some get angry, and others want to debate immigration policy right there on the sidewalk,” he said. “I’m not particularly interested in making artwork that everyone agrees with. If it gets people talking, questioning, or even arguing about what they’re seeing, then I think it’s doing its job.”
